name: Inde Blue
lede: Inde blue is an old dictionary color name for a dark, greyish purple, despite the word blue in it.

sections.title: What the name means
sections.body:
Paterson's dictionary defines *inde blue* as a greyish purple and a dye [1]. The name says blue but the color is purple, and the dictionary also files it among the purples [1]. It sits beside [[indigo]], the great blue dye, [[violet]] and [[purple]], its family [2].

The books say little more about it, and the origin of the name is undocumented here [1]. The Maerz and Paul dictionary of 1930 lists it, and the 1955 ISCC-NBS system, which cites that dictionary, gives the swatch the plain name dark grayish purple [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color near this swatch appears in 79 of them, 0.33 per cent, as photographed [3]. That is rarer than about half of the named colors [3]. It peaks in paintings of the 1900s, at 2.2 times the rate expected from the museums those works come from [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a hidden color, a quiet shadow tone and rarely the subject [3].

origin.source: Paterson, A Dictionary of Colour, "inde blue"

questions.q: Paterson's dictionary defines inde blue as which color?
True or false: inde blue is a blue.

openers: Inde blue is not a blue: the dictionary calls it a greyish purple.
